attempts.sql: WITH sql_database AS (SELECT DISTINCT symbol_id FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile WHERE file_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py' AND name = 'SQLDatabase' AND is_class = true), connector_classes AS (SELECT DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id FROM auto_ontology_code.code.class_bases AS cb JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS c ON c.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id WHERE c.is_class = true AND c.in_test_file = false AND (cb.base_symbol_id IN (SELECT symbol_id FROM sql_database) OR (cb.base_symbol_id IS NULL AND cb.base_name IN ('SQLDatabase', 'base.SQLDatabase')))) SELECT DISTINCT m.enclosing_class_symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, m.name AS method_name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS m JOIN connector_classes AS cc ON m.enclosing_class_symbol_id = cc.class_symbol_id WHERE m.is_method = true AND substr(m.name, 1, 1) <> '_' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS sd WHERE sd.is_method = true AND sd.enclosing_class_symbol_id IN (SELECT symbol_id FROM sql_database) AND sd.name = m.name) ORDER BY class_symbol_id, method_name

request:
The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), method_name (string).
Return exactly the requested output columns, using each requested name as the column alias, in the requested order. Return complete repository-relative file paths and complete symbol IDs exactly as stored. When the question asks which files, symbols or modules, return each distinct one once unless it asks for occurrences.
explanation: This query identifies connector classes that directly inherit from the SQLDatabase class defined in the connectors base module, excluding any class located in test code. It then lists each public method written directly in those connector class bodies, filtering out method names that begin with an underscore and method names already defined by SQLDatabase itself. Results are returned as distinct class-and-method pairs, sorted by class symbol ID and method name.
sql: WITH sql_database AS (SELECT DISTINCT symbol_id FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile WHERE file_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py' AND name = 'SQLDatabase' AND is_class = true), connector_classes AS (SELECT DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id FROM auto_ontology_code.code.class_bases AS cb JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS c ON c.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id WHERE c.is_class = true AND c.in_test_file = false AND (cb.base_symbol_id IN (SELECT symbol_id FROM sql_database) OR (cb.base_symbol_id IS NULL AND cb.base_name IN ('SQLDatabase', 'base.SQLDatabase')))) SELECT DISTINCT m.enclosing_class_symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, m.name AS method_name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS m JOIN connector_classes AS cc ON m.enclosing_class_symbol_id = cc.class_symbol_id WHERE m.is_method = true AND substr(m.name, 1, 1) <> '_' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS sd WHERE sd.is_method = true AND sd.enclosing_class_symbol_id IN (SELECT symbol_id FROM sql_database) AND sd.name = m.name) ORDER BY class_symbol_id, method_name
